Implement a guest-name gate and achievement statistics for this static wedding website. Before editing, inspect the existing code and follow its HTML/CSS/browser-JavaScript patterns. The relevant files are index.html, styles.css, script.js, achievements.js, and README.md.

Requirements

1. Welcome gate
- Add a required guest-name form to the existing welcome screen.
- Keep the “เปิดจดหมาย” (Open Letter) button disabled and visibly greyed out until a non-blank name is submitted. Trim whitespace and validate again when opening the site; do not rely on the button’s disabled state alone.
- After a valid name is submitted, enable the button. Keep the existing welcome animation and responsive design.
- Ensure the existing sessionStorage “opened” behavior cannot skip the name requirement for a new visit or allow an empty name to open the site. Consider how a shared device/browser affects the saved guest name.
- Make the form and button accessible: associated label, keyboard operation, visible focus, and clear validation feedback. Keep the Thai-language UX consistent with the site.

2. Guest identity and honest access limits
- Use the submitted name to associate achievement statistics with a guest.
- A name-only form is not identity verification: guests can enter another name, and client-side gating does not prevent someone from bypassing the welcome screen. Do not describe this as secure authentication. If the requested restriction requires verified identities, explain what additional mechanism is needed rather than implying the name form provides it.

3. Achievement reporting
- When a guest opens the main site, send their name and the current list of unlocked achievement IDs to a new, separately configurable Google Apps Script endpoint. Do not change or reuse the existing RSVP endpoint or disrupt RSVP behavior.
- When an achievement unlocks later, ensure the new unlocked state is eventually reported for that guest. Inspect how achievements are stored and unlocked in achievements.js, and integrate at the shared unlock/state-change point rather than duplicating calls at individual achievement triggers.
- The current RSVP submission can be slow. Avoid blocking the welcome/open flow or achievement UI on analytics requests. Prefer a small, reliable queue that coalesces rapid unlocks into the latest full snapshot, and sends asynchronously. Include reasonable handling for failed requests and page closure; do not silently report success when the endpoint has not confirmed receipt.
- Make reporting idempotent or otherwise safe against retries/duplicate requests. Include an event timestamp and a stable achievement ID list so the host can aggregate unlocked achievements per guest. Do not send RSVP details or unrelated personal data.
- Keep endpoint configuration separate from RSVP_URL. Inspect the existing Apps Script request/CORS conventions and document the expected request/response contract and deployment/setup steps. The Apps Script project is external to this repository; do not claim it has been deployed or change the RSVP Apps Script.

4. Game end time
- The game should stop accepting/reporting new achievement progress after a host-configured deadline.
- No deadline has been supplied yet. Do not invent a date/time. Provide a clearly named, easy-to-configure setting and keep the game open while that setting is unset; document the timezone and required format. When configured, enforce the deadline consistently and give the guest clear feedback.

5. Project quality
- Preserve existing achievement behavior, local progress, RSVP flow, layout, and Thai content.
- Update README.md for the guest-name gate, achievement reporting configuration, external Apps Script contract/setup, and deadline setting.
- Make only the changes needed for these requirements; do not add a framework or unnecessary dependencies.
- Validate the changed behavior with the smallest checks available in the repository. At minimum, verify blank/whitespace names cannot open the gate, a valid name enables it, existing achievement unlocks are reported without blocking the UI, failed reporting does not lose queued state, and an unset/configured deadline behaves as documented.
- In your final response, summarize changed files, validation performed, any external Apps Script work still required, and the limitation that a name field does not authenticate identity.
